key_insight: Urban carbon intensity varies sharply across space and time, so local PV-aware carbon estimates are needed to accurately minimize emissions in building, EV charging, and district energy control.
engineering_relevance: A transferable surrogate model can provide high-resolution carbon intensity estimates from limited municipality/grid inputs, enabling practical deployment in smart city and building energy management.
method: Compute spatial-temporal carbon intensity factors at urban district level from local solar and grid conditions.
Train surrogate models with limited census-grid-cell features to predict these factors.
Compare decision tree-based methods with a neural network architecture for accuracy and transferability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports carbon intensity values ranging from 0 to 316 g/kWh at a summer noon and up to 9% emission estimation error when local variation is ignored.
watch_item: Model accuracy may degrade in less densely built areas or regions with sparse input data, so transferability should be validated before operational use.
paper_title: Quantification and Surrogate Model Estimation of Spatial-Temporal Carbon Intensity Factors
